title: Properness of arbitrary algebraic-space maps tested on schemes
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes [def-weil-size-convention], and let $q:X\to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed with the intrinsic algebraic-space conventions of [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Then $q$ is proper if and only if for every $S$-scheme $T$ and morphism $T\to Y$, the algebraic-space projection $X\times_YT\to T$ is proper. The source $X\times_YT$ is not required to be a scheme. No representability by schemes, Noetherian hypothesis, finite presentation, flatness or quasi-compactness is assumed in advance.

source.place: Tag 083R (lemma-proper-local), equivalence (1) and (2), without the representability-by-schemes specialization.

proof.text: If $q$ is proper, apply [lem-sfb-space-proper-base-change] to every $T\to Y$. It gives properness of $X\times_YT\to T$ for arbitrary algebraic-space sources, exactly as required. That node phrases quasi-compactness of a morphism by quasi-compact scheme atlases of the pullbacks to affine schemes; by [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] such an atlas exists exactly when the point space of the pullback is quasi-compact, which is the quasi-compactness of [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Its separatedness, chartwise local finite type and universal closedness after every algebraic-space base change are literally those of [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties].

Conversely assume the scheme tests. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $V\to Y$ from [def-trf-algebraic-space]; its point map is surjective by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], so the singleton $\{V\to Y\}$ is a jointly surjective etale family. The hypothesis makes $q_V:X_V=X\times_YV\to V$ proper, hence quasi-compact and separated by [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. For every affine $Z\to V$ the point space of $X_V\times_VZ$ is quasi-compact, so by [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] this space has a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme: $q_V$ is quasi-compact in the sense of [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local]. Apply that criterion to the singleton family: $q$ is quasi-compact and separated in its sense. Converting back by [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] for each affine $Z\to Y$, $q$ is quasi-compact and separated in the sense of [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties].

Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $U\to X_V$. Properness of $q_V$ includes local finite type. Apply [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test] first to $q_V$ using the identity chart of $V$ and the chart $U$: $U\to V$ is locally of finite type. Apply the same criterion to $q$ with the charts $V$ and $U$. Thus $q$ is locally of finite type, and together with its quasi-compactness it is of finite type.

source.place: Tag 083R: Tag 040Y (lemma-finite-type-local), the chart criterion; finite type includes quasi-compactness.

proof.text: For universal closedness fix any algebraic space $Z\to Y$, put $E=X\times_YZ$, and choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $p:W\to Z$. The fibre-product property of [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] identifies $E\times_ZW$ with $X\times_YW$. Write $r:E\times_ZW\to E$, $h:E\to Z$, $k:E\times_ZW\to W$. By the scheme-test hypothesis $k$ is proper, hence closed on point spaces by [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. For a closed subset $C\subseteq|E|$, continuity from [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] makes $|r|^{-1}(C)$ closed. Its image $D$ under $|k|$ is closed. That same node gives surjectivity $|E\times_ZW|\to|E|\times_{|Z|}|W|$, so $D=|p|^{-1}(|h|(C))$: each point pair with equal image lifts, and the reverse inclusion follows from commutativity.

source.place: Tag 03IT (lemma-universally-closed-local), (3) implies (4), the surjective-open atlas argument used in Tag 083R.

proof.text: The atlas map $|p|$ is open by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] and surjective, since the atlas is surjective [def-trf-algebraic-space] and the same node turns this into surjectivity of the point map. Consequently $|Z|\setminus|h|(C)=|p|(|W|\setminus D)$ is open. Thus $|h|(C)$ is closed. Since $Z$ and $C$ were arbitrary, $q$ is universally closed. Combine this with separatedness and finite type from steps 2 and 3 and the definition [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties] to conclude properness.

source.place: Tag 03IT, elementary final topological inference; Tag 083R and definition-proper.
